nodes.name: Webhook - Create Variable Product
nodes.notes:
Receives multipart/form-data with:
- Text fields: name, description, categories, brand, tags, regular_price, sale_price, sku, stock_mode, quantity, gallery_count, attributes, variations
- Binary files: product_image, gallery_image_0, gallery_image_1, etc.

Attributes format: JSON array of { id, name, options: [], variation: true, visible: true }
Variations format: JSON array of variation objects with attribute selections, prices, stock config

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Upload Image to WP Media
nodes.notes:
Uploads each image to WordPress Media Library.
Processes ALL items (main image + gallery images + variation images).
Each item's binary 'file' is sent to /wp/v2/media.
Returns the WordPress media object with 'id' for each.

nodes.name: Code - Collect Image IDs & Prepare Tags
HTTP Request - Create or Find Tag
nodes.notes:
Attempts to create each tag. If the tag already exists,
WooCommerce returns a 'term_exists' error with resource_id.
We handle both cases in the next Code node to extract the tag ID.

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Create WooCommerce Product
nodes.notes:
Creates the WooCommerce variable product (parent).
The payload includes: name, type=variable, description,
images (with media IDs), categories, tags, stock config,
and attributes array (used for variations).

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Batch Create Variations
nodes.notes:
Creates ALL variations in a single batch API call.
Endpoint: POST /wp-json/wc/v3/products/{product_id}/variations/batch
Sends { create: [...all variations] } — reduces N calls to 1.
Each variation includes: attributes, regular_price, sale_price, sku, stock config.

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Assign Brand
nodes.notes:
Assigns the brand term to the variable product using the WordPress REST API.
The product custom post type must have the brand taxonomy registered with show_in_rest=true.
The URL uses /wp/v2/product/{id}.
